## Purpose
What happens when a Free workspace uses up its monthly included usage.
## Limits
- Free includes a fixed monthly amount of billed tokens and requests.
- Free has no overage: nothing beyond the included usage is ever charged, and Free workspaces never get an invoice.
## At the limit
Once a Free workspace reaches its monthly limit, further requests are rate-limited: the API returns HTTP `429` with error code `quota_exceeded` and a `Retry-After` header. Requests work again when the next month starts. To keep sending requests sooner, the customer upgrades to a paid plan.

## Overview
Some customers reconcile Redwood token usage against internal estimates and may observe higher usage totals. The most common causes are (1) client retries and (2) streaming cancellation behavior.
This page provides a support-ready explanation and recommended mitigations.
## Key definitions
- **Attempt**: a single request admitted by the Redwood API gateway (server-side).
- **Logical request**: what the customer thinks of as one user action; may map to multiple attempts if the client retries.
## What we bill
### Retries
- Redwood usage is recorded per-attempt.
- If a client retries after a timeout or non-200 response, each admitted attempt can be billable.

For the latest invoice, **August 2026 (INV-BG-202608-009)**, the Hosted API usage cost was **$1,301.46** for Aug 1–15 and **$862.80** for Aug 16–31—**$2,164.26** combined. The invoice total is **$2,595.88**, including **$431.62** for Embeddings.

Your timeout retries could explain higher usage: Redwood records usage per admitted attempt, and an admitted retry can be billable even if the earlier attempt timed out on your side. The six requests linked to these Hosted API lines all returned HTTP 200. I can’t tell from the invoice records alone which were retries of the same logical request, so that’s a plausible explanation, not a confirmed breakdown. The invoice lines also don’t provide a route/model breakdown.

Next, compare the invoice-linked request IDs and their timestamps with your client retry logs to see whether multiple attempts correspond to the same logical request.
So retried attempts are billed as usage too?

Yes—**each retry that Redwood admits can be billed as a separate attempt**, including a retry after a client timeout. If the stream is cancelled, prompt tokens may still count, along with completion tokens generated before cancellation. Each attempt has its own request ID.

So a 10-second timeout on your side doesn’t by itself mean the attempt used zero billable tokens. Comparing your retry logs with request IDs can help confirm which attempts were retries.
